correctness.rationale: For unit vectors, N_lambda^2=max(Q1,Q2) gives (lambda+2)||z||_2^2<=2. Equal-index branch sums are <=2(1+t^2); opposite-index sums are <=2(1+t^2)+4lambda*t/(lambda+2), by exact expansion and Cauchy--Schwarz. Power-mean monotonicity for 1<=p<=2 gives the claimed profile. The explicit diagonal/reflected-diagonal unit pair attains both Q branches and equal output norms, for every t>0. Since lambda*t>0, all maximizers must use a mixed branch; equality in Euclidean norm bounds forces diagonal unit vectors and Cauchy equality forces the opposite diagonal reflection, producing the unique signed symmetry orbit. Symbolic substitution and numerical stress tests checked the identities without substituting for proof.
risks: Rigidity fails at the excluded endpoints lambda=0 or t=0.
The power-mean upper inequality reverses for p>2, so no p>2 claim follows.
All spaces and parameters are real, two-dimensional and strictly positive as stated.

originality.rationale: The defining 2009 article expressly treats the exact Z_lambda quadratic norm but derives only a global comparison estimate and acknowledges inability to get exact values in those examples. The later 2011 full paper supplies only J_{Z_lambda,p}(1), a covered specialization. The new full-scale formula is strictly below the 2009 comparison upper bound for all t!=1, with the exact squared gap lambda(t-1)^2/(lambda+2), and determines the unique maximizing orbit. Targeted statement-level comparisons with the full relevant primary texts and mathematical search results did not reveal a covering theorem. The inaccessible 2006 James paper is a named residual, not proof of noncoverage.
residual_risks: A later paper giving the full J_{Z_lambda,p}(t) function under a different normalized-norm notation could be missing from checked indexes.
Complete text of the Suzuki--Yamano--Kato 2006 James article could not be retrieved from the repository (HTTP 429); its accessible abstract identifies a distinct James minimum invariant.
Indexed literature coverage does not establish uniqueness against unpublished or unindexed mathematics.

value.rationale: The theorem directly closes an exact-value gap stated for the very same Z_lambda space and generalized coefficient in Zuo--Cui 2009, beyond the known t=1 value from Zuo 2011. It replaces a strictly nonsharp off-unit-scale distortion estimate by a sharp closed form for an entire continuous (lambda,t,p) family, with an exact squared slack lambda(t-1)^2/(lambda+2). The maximizing set is structurally rigid for all positive t, and the sharp derivative of the classical modulus detects nonsmoothness despite the Euclidean quadratic component. This is a motivated full invariant profile and equality classification, not a routine t=1 table recomputation.
risks: The calculation is for a two-dimensional max-of-two-quadratics family rather than arbitrary Banach spaces.
Known scalar t=1 results are included only as consistency checks; the value rests on all positive t and equality geometry.
